mappings.note: The top developmental goal of a LANDLESS LABOURER -- the chapter's point that different people want different things from development. C-4.1-LO-1 covers comparing different notions of development. Not LO-2: no income or health indicator is being evaluated.
The aspiration of an educated urban UNEMPLOYED YOUTH -- the same comparison of goals across groups, C-4.1-LO-1.
The correct definition of AVERAGE INCOME. An income indicator being defined, which is the first half of C-4.1-LO-2. Not LO-1: no competing notion of development is at stake, one measure is.

Which of several statements identifies a DEVELOPED country -- the student must hold a working notion of what development means. C-4.1-LO-1. Not LO-2, which would require a specific indicator to be weighed.

Which things money CANNOT buy (freedom from infectious disease, pollution-free air). The whole point is that income alone is an insufficient measure and non-income indicators matter, which is C-4.1-LO-2's 'income AND OTHER indicators'.
What the Human Development Index focuses on -- a composite of income, health and education. C-4.1-LO-2 names exactly those. Not LO-1: the HDI is an indicator, not a competing notion of development.
Why Kerala's infant mortality rate is low -- adequate health and educational facilities. Evaluating a health indicator against its causes, C-4.1-LO-2.

The most promising source of energy fifty years from now AND WHY -- a reasoned prediction about sustainability. Neither LO fits: LO-1 is competing notions of development, LO-2 is income and social indicators, and this chapter's sustainability strand carries no outcome at all. C-4.2 (applies economic reasoning to everyday situations) is the nearest competency. Reported as a frame gap.

Identify the cause that worsens ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION -- the sustainability-of-development strand, which again has no LO in curriculum 106. C-4.2 at competency level. Not C-4.3, which would need data or a policy to evaluate.
Who publishes the Human Development Report (the UNDP) -- recall attached to the HDI apparatus, so C-4.1-LO-2. Not C-4.3: no data or policy is being analysed.
Kerala's literacy rate in 2011 -- an education indicator, C-4.1-LO-2.
The most important component for comparing countries -- average (per capita) income. The income half of C-4.1-LO-2. Not LO-1: the item wants the measure, not a discussion of what development means.
Which state has the lowest infant mortality rate -- a health indicator compared across states, C-4.1-LO-2.
Which country ranks above India on HDI -- the composite indicator used comparatively, C-4.1-LO-2.

What proportion of the country is over-using its groundwater -- resource depletion, the sustainability strand with no LO behind it. C-4.2 at competency level, and reported as a frame gap alongside the other two sustainability items.
How the developmental goals of DIFFERENT SECTIONS of society can be met -- the chapter's argument that goals differ and can conflict. C-4.1-LO-1.
Which statement defines LITERACY RATE -- an education indicator defined, C-4.1-LO-2.

Which is NOT a feature of a developing country -- the developed/developing distinction, i.e. competing notions of development. C-4.1-LO-1. Not LO-2, although income appears among the features; the item tests the category.
The developmental goal of a GIRL FROM A RICH FAMILY -- another group whose goals differ from the labourer's and the industrialist's. C-4.1-LO-1.
The developmental goal of INDUSTRIALISTS -- the same comparison across groups, C-4.1-LO-1.

Which criterion the UNDP uses to measure development -- health, education and income together. The indicator set, C-4.1-LO-2. LO-1 also speaks of 'criteria', but this item names the UNDP's specific measures rather than asking what development should mean.
Which Indian state has the highest HDI -- the composite indicator compared across states, C-4.1-LO-2.
The most important attribute for comparing the development of countries -- income again. C-4.1-LO-2; this is a near-duplicate of an earlier item and is mapped the same way.
Kerala's low infant mortality rate and its cause -- the health indicator explained. C-4.1-LO-2; also a near-duplicate of an earlier item, mapped consistently.
Which levels of the people the HDI compares -- health, education and income. C-4.1-LO-2.
The cause of a high infant mortality rate -- reading behind a health indicator, C-4.1-LO-2. Not C-4.2: no everyday situation is being reasoned about, a standard indicator is being explained.
Which neighbouring country outranks India on human development -- comparative use of the indicator, C-4.1-LO-2.
The term for the proportion of literates aged 7 and above (literacy rate) -- the education indicator named, C-4.1-LO-2.
What per capita income is -- the income indicator defined, C-4.1-LO-2.

Countries with per capita income of US$955 (2017) or less are low-income countries -- the World Bank's income threshold, so the income half of C-4.1-LO-2. LO-1 was considered because a classification is involved, but what is tested is the income figure, not what development means.
